questions.q: What is systemd's job on a Linux server?
options: It is the first program that starts (PID 1); it starts, watches and restarts the other programs
It is a database for logs only
It is a web server like Bazaar's backend
questions.explain: systemd is the manager of all programs. Linux starts it first, as PID 1, and it starts everything else, including your services.

questions.q: Where do you tell systemd which command runs Bazaar's backend?
options: In the ExecStart= line of the unit file bazaar-web.service
questions.explain: The unit file in /etc/systemd/system/ describes the service. ExecStart= is the command to run; User=, EnvironmentFile= and Restart= say how.

questions.q: You ran systemctl start bazaar-web. The server reboots. Is Bazaar running after the reboot?
options: No, not unless you also ran systemctl enable bazaar-web
questions.explain: start runs it now. enable adds it to the list of things systemd starts at boot. On a real server you want both (enable --now does both).

questions.q: Bazaar's backend is killed with kill -9. The unit file has Restart=on-failure and RestartSec=2. What happens?
options: It stays dead until someone logs in
systemd notices, waits 2 seconds, and starts it again with a new PID
questions.explain: The journal shows it: 'Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL', then 'Scheduled restart job, restart counter is at 1', then 'Started bazaar-web.service'.

questions.q: Which command shows the last 20 log lines of Bazaar's service?
questions.explain: journalctl reads the journal. -u picks the unit (service), -n 20 keeps the last 20 lines. The journal files are binary, so cat doesn't work on them.

questions.q: You run systemctl stop bazaar-web. The unit file has Restart=on-failure. What happens?
options: It stops and stays stopped, because a stop on purpose isn't a failure
It can't be stopped while Restart= is set
questions.explain: The journal says 'Deactivated successfully.' and 'Stopped bazaar-web.service'. Restart=on-failure only reacts to crashes and errors.

questions.q: (Going deeper) You fixed a typo in bazaar-web.service, ran systemctl restart, and nothing changed. What did you forget?
options: systemctl daemon-reload, so systemd re-reads unit files from disk
questions.explain: systemd keeps unit files in memory. After editing one, run systemctl daemon-reload, then restart the service. (systemctl edit does the reload for you.)

questions.q: (Going deeper) What does systemctl stop really send to the program first?
options: SIGTERM (a polite 'please exit'), then SIGKILL only if it is still alive after a timeout (90 s by default)
Nothing; it deletes the program's files
questions.explain: SIGTERM first lets a good backend finish the orders it is serving. If it doesn't exit within TimeoutStopSec=, systemd sends SIGKILL.
